κάνναβ-ις , ἡ, gen. ιος
Hdt. 4.74 , εως
Sor. 2.46 , Gal. 6.549 ; acc.
A. “κάνναβιν”
Moschio
ap. Ath. 5.206f , κανναβίδα (sic codd.) Hdt.l.c., Paus. 6.26.6 :—hemp, Cannabis sativa, S. Fr. 243 , Hdt.l.c., Dsc. 3.148 , etc. (but κ. ἀγρία hemp-mallow, Althaea cannabina, ib. 149 ): in pl., -ίδες hemp-seed, Ephipp. 13.6 ; burnt and used to medicate vapour baths, Hdt. 4.75 :—hence κανναβισθῆναι take a vapour-bath, Hsch. (Cf. O E.
hænep 'hemp', Skt. śahás 'a kind of hemp', etc.; borrowed perh. fr. Ugro-Finnish, cf. Čeremissian ke[ndot ]e, ki[ndot ]e 'hemp' and Syrianian pïš 'hemp'.)
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
